title: Wet Burrito
subtitle: A burritto smothered in red chilli sauce and melted cheese
excerpt: A beef burrito topped with a red chilli sauce and a thick layer of melted cheese, then baked until bubbling. Eaten with a fork rather than by hand, and much more satisfying for it.
sourceNotes: Wet burrito (also called a 'smothered burrito'): a regional American dish with strong roots in Michigan and the American Midwest, where it was popularised as a knife-and-fork burrito version in diners and Tex-Mex restaurants. The sauce is typically a red enchilada-style chilli sauce.

recipe.freezeNotes: The assembled wet burrito doesn't freeze well once sauced; the tortilla becomes soggy on defrosting. Freeze the beef filling and sauce separately.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the beef filling and sauce a day ahead and refrigerate. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: A wet burrito is a standard flour-tortilla burrito that has been placed in a baking dish, smothered in red chilli sauce, and topped with cheese before going into the oven. The result is somewhere between an enchilada and a burrito: the tortilla softens under the sauce and the filling bakes together. It's eaten with a fork, not picked up, and it's more generous than either dish it borrows from.

items.prepNote: soaked 20 minutes in boiling water, drained, seeds removed

content.text: A wide, deep roasting dish holds the burritos without them rolling; place them seam-side down so the sauce keeps them closed during baking.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan. Cook {{onion}} finely chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic for 1 minute. Add {{beef-mince}} of beef mince and cook for 5-6 minutes until browned. Stir in the chilli powder and cumin, season with salt, and cook 2 minutes. Stir in the drained black beans and remove from the heat.

Blend the drained ancho chillies, tinned tomatoes, garlic, and cumin until smooth. Pour into a saucepan with {{stock-beef}} of beef stock. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Season with salt.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Spread a ladle of red sauce across the base of a roasting dish.
Warm each flour tortilla in a dry pan. Spoon the beef and bean filling into the lower third of each, add a little cheese, and roll tightly. Place seam-side down in the roasting dish.

Pour the remaining red sauce generously over the burritos; it should cover them. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top. Bake at 190°C for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is golden in places. Rest 5 minutes.
Serve with soured cream spooned alongside and sliced spring onion scattered over the top.

items.symptom: Tortilla falls apart and the filling escapes
items.cause: Burritos placed seam-up, or sauce added too soon
items.fix: Always place burritos seam-side down. The sauce and the weight of the cheese keep them closed.

items.cause: Not enough sauce, or sauce reduced too far before pouring over
items.fix: Use enough sauce to just cover the burritos. The sauce should be pourable; if it's very thick, add a splash of stock.

items.cause: Overfilled, or the tortilla was cold and split on rolling
items.fix: Use 4-5 tablespoons of filling per burrito at most. Warm the tortillas before filling.

items.cause: Pre-grated cheese with anti-caking agent, or cooked too long
items.fix: Grate fresh cheddar and keep the bake to 20-25 minutes. Check at 20 minutes; the cheese should be bubbling and just catching at the edges.

content.text: Wet (or smothered) burritos are particularly associated with Michigan and the Great Lakes states in the US, where Tex-Mex cooking took on a more baked, sauced form that suited cold-climate appetites. They read like enchiladas made with flour tortillas rather than corn, which is exactly what they are. The knife-and-fork format makes them practical for a dinner table in a way a hand-held burrito isn't.
